description: Mask-guided ShapeR fine-tune: held-out Extra% (predicted surface with no matching ground-truth surface nearby) before vs after adding SAM2 foreground-mask conditioning.

modification.option_A: Widen the DINO/ray feature extractor's mask patch-embed conv (dino_ray_extractor._mask_patch_embed[0].proj_in) from Conv2d(1,C,3) to Conv2d(2,C,3): the new input channel carries the SAM2 foreground mask alongside the existing channel.
modification.option_B: Add fg_bias_scale, a single learnable scalar (zero-initialised), used as an attention-bias term scaled by the foreground mask.
modification.backbone: fully frozen; only option A's widened conv weights + option B's scalar are trained

training_config.train_set: 18 diverse objects with GT meshes, NO stools (all stools held out for test)
training_config.wall_time: ~22 min on the SLURM GPU partition used (1 GPU)

single_seed_held_out_result.note: First measurement, single seed, same 8-view SDPA path -- SUPERSEDED by the multi-seed verdict below, kept only for the record.

multiseed_verdict.design: Paired: 5 held-out objects x occlusion levels {0%, 60%} x 3 seeds = 30 paired cells, both models sharing views/masks/noise per cell
multiseed_verdict.result: Mask guidance is NOT better than vanilla ShapeR. No metric at any level has a bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0.
multiseed_verdict.detail: Single-seed hint that guided loses less surface under occlusion (Missing-% degradation +1.6 vs +3.7) did NOT survive at 3 seeds: -2.38 vs -0.36, paired diff -2.02, CI [-5.83, +1.09] -> not supported.
multiseed_verdict.source: updated_shapeR/occlusion_comparison/paired_stats.py output, job 160933 (2026-08-20); folder since superseded/rebuilt under updated_shapeR/testing/, see docs/provenance.md

depth_verified_followup: A later, independent test (see results/D_depth_verified_masks.json) gave the fine-tune a PERFECT ground-truth mask (depth-verified, distractor excluded by construction) instead of a SAM2 guess, isolating whether the mask conditioning channel itself can use an accurate mask. It barely moved Leak% (-0.11 over SAM2's own guess) -- consistent with this section's null verdict: the bottleneck is the model's weak use of the mask channel, not mask quality.
